english: Let $E$ be the ellipse $x^{2}+9y^{2}-2x-36y+28=0$. Let $C$ be the parabola, with axis parallel to the $y$-axis, that passes through both ends of the major axis of $E$ and through the upper end of the minor axis of $E$. If the focus of $C$ is the point $(\alpha,\beta)$, then the value of $\beta$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $E$ दीर्घवृत्त $x^{2}+9y^{2}-2x-36y+28=0$ है। माना कि $C$ वह परवलय है, जिसका अक्ष $y$-अक्ष के समान्तर है, जो $E$ के दीर्घ अक्ष के दोनों सिरों से तथा $E$ के लघु अक्ष के ऊपरी सिरे से होकर जाता है। यदि $C$ की नाभि बिन्दु $(\alpha,\beta)$ है, तो $\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Ends of major axis $(-2,2)$, $(4,2)$; upper end of minor axis $(1,3)$
$C$ has a vertical axis and passes through $(-2,2)$, $(4,2)$, so its axis is $x=1$; $(1,3)$ is on the axis, so it is the vertex: $(x-1)^{2}=-4A(y-3)$
solution_full: Centre $(1,2)$, semi-major axis $3$ along the horizontal line $y=2$, semi-minor axis $1$ along $x=1$.
Ends of the major axis: $(1\pm3,2)$, i.e. $(-2,2)$ and $(4,2)$. Ends of the minor axis: $(1,2\pm1)$; the upper end is $(1,3)$.

A parabola with axis parallel to the $y$-axis is $y=px^{2}+qx+r$. It takes the same value $2$ at $x=-2$ and $x=4$, so its axis is $x=\dfrac{-2+4}{2}=1$. The point $(1,3)$ lies on the axis, so it is the vertex: $C:\ (x-1)^{2}=-4A(y-3)$.
The focus is at distance $A$ below the vertex: $\left(1,3-\dfrac{9}{4}\right)=\left(1,\dfrac{3}{4}\right)$. So $\alpha=1$, $\beta=\dfrac{3}{4}=0.75$.
originality_note: New: a vertical-axis parabola fixed by three special points of a shifted ellipse, where the symmetry of the two major-axis ends makes the minor-axis end the vertex (way 4, a symmetry that removes the three-point solve). Closest known: 'parabola through three given points' and 'reduce a second-degree equation to standard form' exercises. Different because: the points come from the ellipse's own elements, and recognising the vertex replaces solving a 3x3 system.

concept_use.parabola with axis parallel to a coordin: C is written in shifted form (x - 1)^2 = -4A(y - 3) with vertex (1, 3), and its focus is read as (1, 3 - A).
concept_use.ellipse with axis parallel to a coordina: E is reduced to (x - 1)^2/9 + (y - 2)^2/1 = 1 to read its centre and the ends of its major and minor axes.
